A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAGEval and DragonBall. All pages, including appendices, provide readable material that supports comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V4 reports original generation and retrieval experiments, hyperparameter analyses, and human assessments of generated data and automated evaluation.

after.justification: V5 reports original model comparisons, query-type sensitivity analyses, full-dataset retrieval results, and human validation, alongside retained data-quality assessments.

M1.justification: The schema-to-configuration-to-document-to-QRA-to-keypoints pipeline and hybrid rule/LLM generation remain unchanged. V5 adds refinement and generation details without establishing a changed procedure; its after-refinement schema in Figure 10 matches v4 Figure 4.

E1.justification: Both versions use DragonBall's 6,711 questions across finance, law, and medicine in Chinese and English, with the same seven question types and document counts. V5 expands analyses within this retained coverage without introducing new domains, languages, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from eight to nine generators by adding MiniCPM3-4B. In Table 2, GTE-Large and BGE-Large are replaced by GTE-multilingual-Base and MiniCPM-Embedding, substantially revising the retriever comparison set. The zero-shot and one-shot document-generation baselines remain.

E3.justification: The main setup changes from language-specific BGE-Large to BGE-M3, increases maximum generated tokens from 256 to 512, and replaces first-50 selection with random sampling. TopK changes from 2/4/6 to 2/5/8, and chunk/TopK configurations also change. V5 adds BLEU and full-dataset retrieval evaluation while omitting EIR from the TopK comparison. Automated-metric validation changes from 420 questions to 210, with three annotators per question and voting.

E4.justification: V4's aggregate chunk-size and English scenario comparisons are replaced by detailed question-type sensitivity analyses across all six domain/language combinations in v5 Tables 7–12. Figure 3 now compares factual, multi-hop, and numerical questions. TopK analysis and human validation are revised, while the earlier chunk-size hallucination and irrelevance results are no longer reported.

E5.justification: V5 Appendix C newly reports Fleiss' kappa of 0.7686 for three independent annotators and documents voting. This adds statistical agreement reporting; neither version reports confidence intervals or repeated-run uncertainty for the model comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 contain extensively replaced results under revised settings. For example, GPT-4o Completeness changes from 51.87/68.45 to 79.13/69.36 for CN/EN; this is not a controlled performance improvement. V5 adds MiniCPM3-4B and BLEU entries, full-dataset retrieval scores, question-type breakdowns, and revised human–LLM validation results. The QRA-quality scores and document-generation comparison results are retained.

T1.justification: The definitions and equations for Recall, EIR, Completeness, Hallucination, and Irrelevancy remain mathematically equivalent. V5 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: scenario-specific dataset generation, factual-keypoint evaluation metrics, and DragonBall-based assessment. V5's explicit references to automation and superiority over ROUGE-L/BLEU restate capabilities and claims already present in v4.

C2.justification: V5 adds explanations for BM25's keyword-matching advantage, diminishing returns and possible noise risks from larger TopK, and question-specific configuration choices. These replace much of v4's language- and scenario-level interpretation. The limitations also lose substantive discussions of synthetic-data realism, document-length constraints on long-context testing, and commercial applicability.

D1.justification: V5 substantially expands documentation through schema normalization and hierarchical/modular generation details in Appendices A–B, an abbreviated evaluator prompt in Figure 15, FlashRAG/vLLM identification, and dated GPT model identifiers. It omits v4's explicit fp16 and nonoverlapping-chunk disclosures. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding implementation changes; the code/data link and license remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds citations for FlashRAG, vLLM, scaling laws, ROUGE, BLEU, and multilingual GTE, while removing works including RAGBench, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and KILT. Related work sharpens the contrast between fixed benchmarks and adaptable scenario-specific evaluation, while retaining the same basic positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Retrieval and hyperparameter analyses are reorganized under Section 4.3, appendices receive separate refinement/generation/assessment/examples sections, and the limitations are heavily condensed. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains model and BLEU columns/entries, Table 3 becomes a TopK-only display, and Figure 3 replaces domain curves with question-type curves. V5 adds Tables 6–12, a pre-refinement schema figure, and an evaluator-prompt figure, and redraws the human–machine comparison. Retained examples and quality-assessment displays are substantially relocated.

improvement.justification: V5 improves technical assessability through expanded implementation explanations, a partial evaluator prompt, detailed query-type analyses, and explicit three-annotator validation with agreement reporting. These gains are tempered by removing v4's useful realism and long-context caveats. Appendix C also leaves unclear how its reported 1.67% human–LLM difference relates to Figure 7, limiting the strength of the validation improvement.
